contradicting_evidence: Stablecoin contraction across daily, weekly and monthly windows, together with weak mid-alt participation, provides a coherent downside argument that could persist.
Positive latest-session ETF flows and preceding ETH outperformance provide a recovery argument if they develop into sustained demand and broader participation.
The sharp latest hourly decline is a genuine short-horizon directional signal, although its persistence over a week is unproven.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: No defensible net weekly direction can be assigned. Further weakness, stabilization and recovery attempts are all compatible with the supplied evidence. Broad recovery requires observable transmission beyond BTC and ETH; persistent contraction requires more than one sharp hourly decline. Current vulnerability remains elevated without a supported weekly destination.
falsification_conditions: A sustained sequence of higher prices, stronger ETH/BTC, broader positive participation and repeated positive settled flows would establish an upside case and invalidate the no-edge assessment.
Repeated lower prices accompanied by persistent negative participation and renewed settled outflows would establish a downside case and invalidate the no-edge assessment.
A durable, repeatedly observed range with stable participation would support a sideways forecast rather than an unresolved directional assessment.
missing_evidence: Recent daily trend structure and repeated observations demonstrating whether recovery or deterioration persists.
Updated multi-session institutional flows and evidence that available stablecoin liquidity is being deployed.
Confirmed broad-alt participation, full small-cap coverage and microcap observations; these cannot be inferred from Top-100 proxies.
supporting_evidence: The principal evidence spans different cadences: one acute hourly selloff, an earlier rolling 24h breadth snapshot, one latest ETF session and slower liquidity observations. These do not establish a reliable weekly path.
Latest settled institutional flows are positive while stablecoin supply is contracting, leaving demand and liquidity signals in conflict.

The 30d altseason measure shows only 9 of 49 constituents outperforming BTC, but the longer-window measures are less uniformly weak; this describes uneven participation, not a timed weekly transition.
BTC dominance is a single settled daily observation, while ETH's preceding 24h outperformance has not transmitted into positive returns across the observed capitalization buckets.
